enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

1102 AM MST Mon Nov 2 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1102 AM MST Mon Nov 2 2026

 - Dry weather through this weekend with some afternoon breezes
   returning for Wednesday.

 - Temperatures will run near to slightly below normal through the
   upcoming week.  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1102 AM MST Mon Nov 2 2026

A period of quiet weather expected across the Borderland for the
next week. Models in good agreement in transitioning from a
current northwest flow to a persistent westerly flow pattern. This
will keep moisture out of the area with just an occasional breezy
day. For this evening, winds will gradually decrease as upper low
moves into the Central/Southern Plains and gradient relaxes. Much
lower dew points will be moving in so mostly clear skies by mid
evening. One small concern is potential for fog in the morning due
to recent rains, but winds will not go completely calm and could
just result in very patchy fog. Looks like a good hard freeze in
the Mimbres River Valley of the Gila region where lows in the mid
to upper 20s look likely. 

For Tue, a shortwave ridge moves into the west with lighter winds
and mostly sunny skies. H85 temps warm to around 16-18C and with
full sun, should get good mixing. NBM temps looked about 3-5
degrees too cool for highs and MET/MAV guidance also agree with
highs being warmer. So did go ahead and raise highs closer to MOS
guidance numbers. Same thing for Wed, which should have even
better mixing with west winds increasing to 10-15mph. NBM temps
seemed about 5 degrees too cool and again warmed up closer to MOS
guidance.  

There will be a shortwave moving well to our north Wed night into
Thu which will cool temps down a few degrees. NBM temps looked
more reasonable here and didn't adjust much. Persistent weather
into the weekend as an upper low cuts off of Baja and low level
easterly flow keeps temps near to slightly below normal. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1102 AM MST Mon Nov 2 2026

P6SM FEW-BKN040-060 cloud deck will gradually be dissipating
through the afternoon as drier air moves in. By just after sunset,
skies will become SKC-FEW250. Winds will be westerly at
15-25G35KTS, slightly stronger in the Sac Mts through the
afternoon and decrease gradually through the evening hours.  

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1102 AM MST Mon Nov 2 2026

Besides the winds through this afternoon, fire weather concerns
will be minimal for the next week. Zonal flow through the end of
the week will bring in drier air and near to slightly below normal
temperatures. Even with the drier air moving in, min RH's will
stay above 25-30%. No chances for precipitation for the upcoming
work week and likely beyond. Vent rates will be poor Tuesday, but
some breezy conditions Wed will result in Fair to Good rates. 

&&
